nodes.content: Build an incremental interprocedural alias analysis that preserves soundness across pointer escapes, indirect calls, and changing function summaries.
requirements: Soundly handle heap objects, pointer casts, recursion, and opaque external calls under documented IR semantics.
After single-function edits, match full recomputation’s alias answers while reducing median analysis latency by 50%.

nodes.content: Use SCC-fixed-point, versioned points-to summaries with escape-aware heap abstractions, conservative cast/unknown-call effects, and reverse-dependency invalidation for summary/indirect-target changes.
How are callers invalidated when an edit adds a previously absent indirect callee through an escaped heap function pointer?
Watching heap locations feeding indirect callsites, even with empty target sets, preserves full-recomputation alias answers after new targets appear.
Test watched-location invalidation on escaped-pointer edits, then implement SCC summaries; benchmark alias equivalence and ≥50% median-latency reduction.
Run EscapedCallback-64 edits adding escaped-heap function-pointer stores to targetless callsites; compare watched-invalidation and full-recomputation alias matrices.
EscapedCallback-64 showed 3/64 alias-matrix mismatches: newly cast-reachable feeder locations lacked watches, leaving indirect callees stale.
Version cast-reachability dependencies and re-register feeder watches before propagating indirect targets; predict 64/64 EscapedCallback-64 alias-matrix matches.
Implement versioned cast-reachability watches and rerun EscapedCallback-64, comparing post-edit indirect-target sets and alias matrices against full recomputation.
EscapedCallback-64 achieved 64/64 matching alias matrices and indirect-target sets after versioned cast-reachability watches replaced stale dependencies.
Replace location-only watches after three mismatches with versioned cast-reachability watches; EscapedCallback-64 now matches 64/64 alias matrices.
Implement versioned SCC points-to summaries with reverse dependencies for caller and indirect-target changes, plus conservative heap, cast, and opaque-call effects.
IncrementalAlias v0.1 implements versioned SCC summaries, reverse invalidation, cast-reachability watches, and conservative escaped-heap and opaque-call effects.
How do newly introduced recursive call edges trigger SCC rebuilding and caller invalidation without retaining stale points-to facts?
Use differential points-to propagation with provenance-tracked retractions and affected-SCC rebuilding when edits alter recursive or indirect call edges.
First establish sound retraction-provenance and SCC-rebuilding invariants; only then enable differential propagation and benchmark alias equivalence and latency.
Instrument IncrementalAlias v0.1 with provenance and affected-SCC rebuild checks; test recursive-edge edits against full recomputation on RecursionEdit-80.
RecursionEdit-80 harness instruments IncrementalAlias v0.1 to log retraction provenance, SCC rebuild boundaries, and alias differences against full recomputation.
Prototype differential retractions in IncrementalAlias v0.1; run RecursionEdit-80 against versioned-summary baseline and full recomputation, auditing harness traces.
RecursionEdit-80: differential retractions matched 80/80 full-recomputation alias matrices; median latency was 38 ms versus 82 ms baseline, 105 ms full.
Adopt differential retractions alongside cast-reachability watches: RecursionEdit-80 matched 80/80 at 38 ms median versus 105 ms full recomputation.
Implement call-edge change detection, rebuild affected SCCs, retract obsolete points-to facts by provenance, and invalidate transitive callers.
RecursionEdit-80: versioned summaries retained stale aliases on 6/80 cycle-breaking edits; provenance retraction matched full recomputation.
How can retractions preserve points-to facts supported by another recursive path when an edited call edge splits an SCC?
Recompute rebuilt SCCs from surviving base constraints, then propagate fact deltas; predict 48/48 alias-matrix matches on SplitCycle-48.
Track base-rooted derivation witnesses per fact; after SCC splits, retract only facts lacking surviving witnesses, predicting 48/48 SplitCycle-48 matches.
Use demand-driven, dependency-tracked alias queries with conservative unknown-call effects, recomputing only dirty query slices after edits.
How can cached query slices detect newly reachable opaque calls whose effects were absent when the slices were built?
Instrument call-reachability watches in cached slices; run SplitCycle-48 with newly reachable opaque calls, comparing SCC-rebuild and witness-based retractions.
SplitCycle-48: SCC rebuilding matched 48/48 alias matrices, including newly reachable opaque calls; witness retraction retained cycle-supported aliases in 4/48.
Run OpaqueFrontier-40 edits exposing external callees through casts; compare cached-slice invalidation and witness retractions against full recomputation.
OpaqueFrontier-40: rooted-witness retractions matched 12/12 SCC splits exposing cast-reachable opaque calls; watched query slices matched 40/40.
At what queried-pointer coverage do dirty query slices become slower than differential SCC propagation after single-function edits?
On QueryCoverage-120, dirty slices will exceed differential SCC median latency once queried-pointer coverage reaches 40%.
Using validated SCC rebuilding and watched slices, compare QueryCoverage-120 median edit latencies against differential propagation at 20%, 40%, 60% coverage.
QueryCoverage-120 median latency: dirty slices took 24/47/66 ms at 20/40/60% coverage, versus differential SCC’s 39/40/41 ms.
Use watched query slices below 40% coverage; switch to SCC rebuilding otherwise, preserving opaque-call invalidation and cycle-split correctness.
Use epoch-stamped IR-effect dependencies to invalidate cast, escape, indirect-target, and opaque-call effects atomically before rebuilding affected SCCs.
Integrate epoch-stamped effects with the coverage switch, validate alias equivalence across mixed edits, then benchmark median latency against full recomputation.
Extend the RecursionEdit-80 harness with epoch-stamped effect logs; test mixed cast, escape, indirect-call, and SCC-split edits against full recomputation.
MixedEffect-96 revises the RecursionEdit-80 harness with epoch-effect logs and full-recomputation comparisons for cast, escape, indirect-call, and SCC-split edits.
Run both harnesses on RecursionEdit-80, checking identical alias-difference reports; exercise MixedEffect-96 epoch logs against full recomputation.
Both harnesses agreed on 80/80 RecursionEdit-80 reports; MixedEffect-96 matched full-recomputation alias matrices on 96/96 edits.
Benchmark epoch-stamped analysis with the coverage switch on MixedEffect-96, recording alias-matrix equivalence and median edit latency versus full recomputation.
MixedEffect-96 benchmark harness adds coverage-switch decisions, per-edit latency traces, and alias-matrix comparisons to the epoch-effect logs.
Cross-check revised and original MixedEffect-96 alias reports; audit coverage-switch traces and benchmark median edit latency against full recomputation.
MixedEffect-96: both harnesses matched 96/96 alias matrices; coverage-switch latency was 42 ms median versus 105 ms full recomputation.
Adopt epoch-stamped coverage switching after validated MixedEffect-96 equivalence: 96/96 alias matches, 42 ms versus 105 ms median.
How can alias queries avoid observing mixed epochs when one edit changes cast reachability and indirect-call targets together?
Pin queries to committed immutable summary epochs; atomically publish cast and indirect-target updates, predicting zero mixed-epoch answers in ConcurrentEdit-128.
Extend MixedEffect-96 into ConcurrentEdit-128; interleave paired cast/indirect edits with queries, comparing pinned answers against committed full-recomputation snapshots.
ConcurrentEdit-128 recorded zero mixed-epoch answers across 128 interleavings; every pinned query matched its committed full-recomputation snapshot.
Specify executable IR semantics for allocation-site heaps, pointer casts, escapes, and opaque-call havoc; validate with generated differential tests.
Using validated coverage switching and pinned epochs, formalize heap/cast/escape/opaque-call rules; generate oracle-checked edits and benchmark alias equivalence and latency.
Codify heap, cast, escape, and opaque-call rules in IncrementalAlias; extend MixedEffect-96 with bounded-interpreter differential tests.
IRSemantics v0.2 specifies allocation-site heaps, address-preserving casts, unknown-cast top, transitive escapes, and opaque-call reachable-memory havoc, with a bounded-interpreter oracle.
Run SemanticsFuzz-256 generated edits with pinned epochs; compare incremental and full alias answers against bounded-interpreter may-alias witnesses.
SemanticsFuzz-256: incremental matched full alias matrices on 256/256 edits; neither missed any of 1,842 bounded-interpreter alias witnesses.
Adopt IRSemantics v0.2 with differential SCC retractions and epoch-stamped coverage switching; SemanticsFuzz-256 matched 256/256 edits without missed witnesses.
